answer.sourceLine: It is Piglet’s line, spoken to Rabbit in Chapter VII of Winnie-the-Pooh (1926), as Rabbit recruits him for the scheme to kidnap Baby Roo. The wording is confirmed word-for-word in the Project Gutenberg text ↗; the popular short form simply drops the interruption “said Piglet, sniffing slightly.”

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: VII — “In Which Kanga and Baby Roo Come to the Forest, and Piglet Has a Bath”
14 October 1926 · Methuen & Co., London, and E. P. Dutton, New York

source.excerpt:
“Piglet,” said Rabbit, taking out a pencil, and licking the end of it, “you haven’t any pluck.”

“It is hard to be brave,” said Piglet, sniffing slightly, “when you’re only a Very Small Animal.”

Rabbit, who had begun to write very busily, looked up and said:

“It is because you are a very small animal that you will be Useful in the adventure before us.”

Piglet was so excited at the idea of being Useful, that he forgot to be frightened any more…
trail: The sentence appears verbatim in Chapter VII of the Project Gutenberg text of Winnie-the-Pooh ↗ (eBook #67098): “It is hard to be brave,” said Piglet, sniffing slightly, “when you’re only a Very Small Animal.”

Wikiquote ↗ lists the full sentence — interruption and all — under its Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) heading, sourced to Chapter Seven. It names no speaker there; the speaker comes from the Gutenberg text itself, which prints “said Piglet” inside the sentence. The condensed form in our headline is our own clipping, not Wikiquote’s.
Wikipedia ↗ dates first publication to 14 October 1926 — Methuen & Co. in England, E. P. Dutton in the United States, illustrated by E. H. Shepard.
The Smithsonian Libraries scan ↗ is copy no. 42 of the 1926 E. P. Dutton large-paper issue, one of 200 numbered copies signed by author and illustrator.

source.rightsNote: Winnie-the-Pooh was first published in 1926, and Duke’s Center for the Study of the Public Domain ↗ records that it entered the US public domain on 1 January 2022 with the rest of that year’s copyrights. Only the 1926 book is covered by that finding. Duke’s 2022 note flagged that later Pooh material was still restricted at the time — The House at Pooh Corner (1928), the book that introduces Tigger, followed it into the US public domain on 1 January 2024. Disney’s Pooh films and character designs remain separately protected.
source.useLine: Free to use in the US, including in commercial and paid presentations — no permission or licence needed. Outside the US it is not so simple: Milne died on 31 January 1956, so in life-plus-70 countries (UK/EU) the 1926 text stays in copyright until 1 January 2027. Check your jurisdiction before publishing.

author.name: A. A. Milne
author.heading: A. A. Milne
author.bio: Alan Alexander Milne joined the staff of Punch in 1906 and rose to assistant editor, then served as a signals officer on the Somme in 1916 before being invalided out with trench fever. He wrote Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) and The House at Pooh Corner (1928) around his young son Christopher Robin, and spent much of the rest of his life uneasy about it — he complained that “the legal Christopher Robin” had already had more publicity than he wanted for him. He was a working playwright and novelist first; the bear made him immortal and slightly resentful about it.

misattribution.heading: What goes wrong with it
misattribution.intro: The quotation itself is real — unusually so for a Pooh line. But three things routinely go wrong with it in circulation.

items.why: Memes, mugs and nursery prints regularly put the line in the bear’s mouth. It is Piglet’s, said to Rabbit — the 1926 text ↗ prints “said Piglet” inside the sentence itself. In the run-up to it Pooh has been off in a corner practising saying “Aha!” — he is not part of the exchange at all.

The book prints “It is hard to be brave,” said Piglet, sniffing slightly, “when you’re only a Very Small Animal.” The circulating form drops the sniff, and a widely shared variant opens with “It’s hard” — the 1926 text ↗ reads “It is.”

The far more viral Pooh line about courage is Christopher Robin’s in Disney’s 1997 direct-to-video Pooh’s Grand Adventure ↗, written by Karl Geurs and Carter Crocker. Searching the Project Gutenberg texts of Winnie-the-Pooh and The House at Pooh Corner returns no occurrence of it in either book.

misattribution.truthLine: The real line is Piglet’s, in Chapter VII of Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) ↗ — and Rabbit’s reply is the half everyone leaves off: “It is because you are a very small animal that you will be Useful in the adventure before us.”

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The scene is not an inspirational poster. Rabbit has drawn up a plan to kidnap Baby Roo, Piglet raises the sensible objection that a mother kangaroo deprived of her young might turn dangerous, and Rabbit — taking out a pencil and licking the end of it — tells him flatly, “you haven’t any pluck.” The line is Piglet’s reply: an admission of cowardice offered as a fact about his size.

What makes it stick is Rabbit’s answer, which almost never travels with it. Rather than telling Piglet to be braver, Rabbit reframes the smallness as the qualification: it is because he is a very small animal that he will be useful. Piglet is so pleased at the idea of being Useful that he forgets to be frightened. Milne, who had been a signals officer on the Somme, gave his smallest character a fear that is never argued away — only given a job.
detailsBody: Piglet returns to the same self-description two chapters later, alone and marooned: “It’s a little Anxious,” he said to himself, “to be a Very Small Animal Entirely Surrounded by Water.” The capitalised phrase is a running label Milne uses for him, not a one-off.

Rabbit’s notes on the plan, printed a few pages later, include the line: “A Thought. If Roo had jumped out of Kanga’s pocket and Piglet had jumped in, Kanga wouldn’t know the difference, because Piglet is a Very Small Animal.”

sourcesVerified.claim: Chapter VII of Winnie-the-Pooh contains verbatim: "It is hard to be brave," said Piglet, sniffing slightly, "when you're only a Very Small Animal." — followed by Rabbit's reply about being Useful. The chapter title is "In Which Kanga and Baby Roo Come to the Forest, and Piglet Has a Bath." The texts of Winnie-the-Pooh and The House at Pooh Corner contain no occurrence of "braver than you believe" or "smarter than you think."
Project Gutenberg eBook #67098 is Winnie-the-Pooh by A. A. Milne, illustrated by Ernest H. Shepard, listed as public domain in the USA.

Wikiquote lists the full sentence — "It is hard to be brave," said Piglet, sniffing slightly, "when you're only a Very Small Animal." — under its Winnie-the-Pooh (1926) heading, sourced to "Chapter Seven." with no speaker suffix. The condensed popular form is not what Wikiquote prints, and the literal token "- Piglet" appears on the page only on the Chapter Nine entry.

Winnie-the-Pooh was first published 14 October 1926 by Methuen & Co. in England and E. P. Dutton in the United States, illustrated by E. H. Shepard, and entered the US public domain on 1 January 2022.

Duke's Center for the Study of the Public Domain states that copyrighted works from 1926 entered the US public domain on 1 January 2022, and names A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh among them, with the caveat that subsequent Pooh stories and adaptations (e.g. Tigger, introduced 1928) are not covered.

The Internet Archive item is the 1926 E. P. Dutton large-paper edition of Winnie-the-Pooh, limited to 200 numbered and signed copies; the digitised copy is number 42, signed by author and illustrator, contributed by Smithsonian Libraries and fully viewable.

Pooh's Grand Adventure: The Search for Christopher Robin is a 1997 Disney film written by Carter Crocker and Karl Geurs, and contains Christopher Robin's line "You're braver than you believe, and stronger than you seem, and smarter than you think."

A. A. Milne was born 18 January 1882 and died 31 January 1956; he joined the staff of Punch in 1906 and became assistant editor, served as a signals officer on the Somme in 1916 and contracted trench fever, published Winnie-the-Pooh in 1926 and The House at Pooh Corner in 1928, and said "I feel that the legal Christopher Robin has already had more publicity than I want for him."

Quote Investigator's A. A. Milne category page lists investigations of other Milne-attributed sayings (including "Sometimes I Sits and Thinks, and Sometimes I Just Sits") and contains no article on "hard to be brave" or "Very Small Animal."
